predictions.directional_claim: mainstream retail adoption expands beyond specialty fitness retailers into mass-market sporting goods
predictions.observable_check: weighted/rucking vest listings appear under a house label at Target, Walmart or Dick's Sporting Goods in those retailers' own online catalogs, in the 12-20 lb range, at two or more of the three
predictions.reasoning: Four independent sources converge: a first-person community observation of local stockouts, four consecutive weeks on Amazon's Sports & Outdoors movers list still dominated by specialty brands, a breakout Google related query with inland regional spread, and lifestyle coverage reframing low-intensity walking as the successor to HIIT. Cultural relevance is high because the styling searches are outrunning the equipment searches, which historically precedes a category leaving the gym; white space is real because the mass-market labels are absent from the movers list today; plausibility is strong because the enabling behavior (walking) needs no skill acquisition; evidence breadth spans commerce, search, social and press; cross-category potential shows in the apparel styling searches; consumer interest is already measurable rather than projected.
predictions.angle: Walking is being reclassified as training rather than recovery, and the vest is the object that makes the reclassification visible to everyone else on the trail.
predictions.audience_question: Would you wear a weighted vest on an ordinary walk around your neighborhood?

predictions.directional_claim: displaces ricotta as the default soft cheese in home-cooked savory dishes
predictions.observable_check: at least two of Great Value, Good & Gather and 365 by Whole Foods list a full-fat cottage cheese tub at 4% milkfat or higher in their own online grocery catalogs, merchandised under a cooking or cheese category rather than yogurt
predictions.reasoning: A structural-enabling change plus a pattern break: private-label lines adding higher-fat tubs aimed at cooking is a supply-side condition, and full-fat SKUs outgrowing low-fat ones inverts the category's long-standing diet framing. Cultural relevance sits in the protein-first home-cooking identity; white space is the cooking set, where the category is not merchandised today; plausibility is high because the substitution is cheaper and needs no new technique; evidence breadth is narrower than the vest call, which is why confidence is lower; cross-category potential reaches into baking; consumer interest shows in creator recipe content rather than in search yet.

The wellness press cluster is real and sustained, and I am fairly confident something is happening here, but the coverage names no specific ingredient, product or measurable behavior, so I cannot state what changes or how anyone would check it.
